label: prf:local-substrate-q
title: Proof of Local Value of the Substrate Parameter
html:
The algebraic topological mass formula (algebraic topological mass) gives the mass ratio in \mathbb{Q}(q) as m_\mu / m_e = \Phi_1(4_1) / \hbar_q^{2}. Here \Phi_1(4_1) = \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(\mathrm{Vol}_q(4_1)) is the \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}-image of the algebraic quantum volume (def:algebraic-quantum-volume) and \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1}. The Archimedean form of this identity (topological mass formula) applies \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}. This equates \Phi_1(4_1) with the hyperbolic volume \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) at q = q_0 via the volume conjecture [kashaev1997, murakami-murakami2001] as \tau-side naming. Substituting the \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}-specialised numerical value yields:

  (1 - q^{-1})^{2}
  = \frac{2.02988}{206.7683}
  \approx 0.009817,
  \qquad
  1 - q^{-1} \approx 0.09908,
  \qquad
  q \approx 1.10998.

The SnapPy witness (knot volumes verification) independently verifies the numerical values. It computes q \approx 1.10998 from \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) \approx 2.02988321281931 and m_\mu/m_e \approx 206.768 (CODATA 2022). The function f(q) = (1 - q^{-1})^{2} is strictly increasing for q > 1 and maps (1,\infty) onto (0,1). Thus the root is unique. The \pm0.001 uncertainty propagates from the CODATA relative uncertainty (2.2 \times 10^{-8} on m_\mu / m_e) and the \tau-image SnapPy error bound (10^{-14} on \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)). Finite decimal truncation of q provides the dominant contribution. This value aligns with the hadronic mass predictions of terminal resolution and the q-deformed Hall conductance corrections of photonic Hall effect.
